method: Every one of the 18 gender + 21 singular proposals judged individually; no sampling. Beyond SAOL/SO judgement of each value I ran four structural tests the first round could not run on itself: (1) SISTER-KEY DUP TEST — reconstructed every corrected row and diffed it against all 1263 keys; (2) COUPLING TEST — for every gender proposal, checked whether the same key's plural was also corrected, and where it was not, whether it was HELD (held-sv.json) rather than overlooked; (3) MECHANISM TEST — re-implemented genderSv's SV_ETT_WORDS/SV_ETT_SUFFIXES lookup from scripts/build-image-vocabulary.js and re-ran it on every disputed word, to test the reviewers' stated causes instead of believing them; (4) CITATION TEST — checked each src for the German 'hot' pattern (a guessed value with an empty src). conflicts-sv.json is empty: no proposal in this slice overturns a shipped native gender decision.

NOTE for the operator, NOT an objection: this row is ALREADY byte-identical to key 'parasol' ({Parasoll,Parasollar,n}, both themes=[beach]) and stays identical after the fix. STRONGEST CORROBORATION IN THIS SLICE, and it is external to the reviewer's reasoning. SAOL: chips subst. ~et, pl. ~ — ett chips, chipset ('han åt ett enda chips'). Decisive: the sister key 'potato-chips' ALREADY SHIPS THE IDENTICAL WORD 'Chips' with g='t'. So the same word currently carries two different genders in the same file ({Chips,Chips,n} vs {Chips,Chips,t}) — the data contradicts itself, and this fix resolves the contradiction rather than creating one. Note the 't' on potato-chips cannot have come from genderSv (identical input string -> identical output), so it is a surviving human value. NOT pluralia tantum (I tested the operator's warning): 'ett chips' is a live singular, so the gender code is meaningful. NO COUPLING GAP: p='Chips' is the correct neuter zero plural.

VALUE IS RIGHT, but I record two defects in the proposal itself. Value: Swedish dinosaur genus names are utrum (en tyrannosaurus, en velociraptor, en triceratops); *ett deinonychus is impossible. VERIFIED, not assumed: 23 of the 25 dinosaur keys in this data already carry 'n' — only deinonychus and parasaurolophus carry 't'. MECHANISM VERIFIED by re-running the script: 'deinonychus' ends in the letters h-u-s and 'hus' IS in SV_ETT_SUFFIXES, so the ett-suffix rule mis-fired; 'allosaurus'/'stegosaurus'/'triceratops' match nothing and correctly got 'n'. That is why exactly these two of 25 broke. DEFECT 1 — FALSE CITATION: src='SAOL', but SAOL has no entry for 'deinonychus'; this citation cannot be honoured and should be downgraded to the principle-plus-sibling-consistency basis its own twin used honestly (parasaurolophus: src=''). DEFECT 2 — COUPLING GAP, the only genuine one I found: the false 'hus' match also suppressed the plural (p='Deinonychus'), so applying the gender alone yields 'en deinonychus -> flera deinonychus', an utrum noun with a zero plural. Its identical twin parasaurolophus HAS its plural held in held-sv.json; deinonychus's plural is neither corrected NOR held. Recommend adding deinonychus.plural to held alongside parasaurolophus before this is applied.

SAOL: fikon subst. ~et — ett fikon, fikonet, flera fikon. MECHANISM VERIFIED: 'fikon' matches nothing in either list -> default 'n', and the same miss produced the invented 'Fikonar'. Textbook camp-class coupled defect. Coupling intact (Fikonar->Fikon filed).

I CHECKED THE APPARENT COUPLING GAP AND IT IS NOT ONE: the plural is absent from corrections because it is deliberately HELD in held-sv.json ('the defect is certain; only the replacement form is uncertain — Trädgårdsgrepar or Trädgårdsgreper, I cannot verify which from memory'). I TESTED THIS AGAINST THE GERMAN 'hot' PATTERN THE OPERATOR FLAGGED, AND IT IS NOT THAT PATTERN — the empty src here is honesty, not a guess. Three disanalogies: (1) 'hot' is an ADJECTIVE, which has no lexical gender at all, so 'n' there was as invented as 'm'; 'parasaurolophus' is a NOUN and has a real gender that can be determined. (2) Fixing 'hot' corrected 1 of 22 identical adjectives AWAY from the rest, making the data LESS consistent; here 23 of 25 dinosaur keys already carry 'n' (I enumerated them), so this fix moves 2 outliers TOWARD the set and makes the data MORE consistent. (3) The empty src is the correct entry: SAOL has no 'parasaurolophus' lemma, so no SAOL citation is possible, and the reviewer declined to fabricate one — unlike this key's own twin deinonychus, which claims src='SAOL' for the identical unlistable claim (flagged there). MECHANISM VERIFIED: 'parasaurolophus' ends in the letters h-u-s and 'hus' is in SV_ETT_SUFFIXES -> false 't'. SAOL spells the shrub 'syren', without the acute. The accent belongs to Swedish loans in stressed -é (idé, armé, kafé, trofé), not to stressed -en (cf. hygien, siren) — so 'Syrén' applies an -é rule to an -en word. themes=[flowers] fix the shrub reading. No homonym risk: 'syre' (oxygen) is neuter with the definite 'syret', so it cannot collide with 'en syren'. Pure spelling fix of the same lemma, not a lemma change. Coupling intact (Syrénar->Syrener).

THIS IS A LEMMA SELECTION, NOT A FORM FIX — the brief's definition of ESCALATE ('lemmabyte'), and it carries the German 'lego' risk the operator named: a 'correction' that deletes an attested form. The current row {s:Muffin, p:Muffins, g:n} IS broken — 'Muffins' as the plural of a Swedish lemma 'muffin' is an English -s plural, not a Swedish form — so something must change. But there are TWO coherent resolutions: (a) the proposal's s=Muffins / p=Muffins (the English plural borrowed as the Swedish singular, the keps<caps and kex<cakes pattern), or (b) s=Muffin / p=Muffiner. Choosing between them decides which lemma the file uses, and the usage is genuinely split. I CANNOT VERIFY from memory whether SAOL also lists 'muffin' as an accepted variant, and if it does, the proposal deletes an attested form — exactly what happened to 'lego' in the German round. The proposal does not establish that 'muffin' is unattested; it argues only that 'muffins' is attested, which does not settle it. The src is itself hedged ('SAOL lemma muffins; Språkrådet recommends...') rather than the verbatim citation shape this reviewer uses everywhere else ('SAOL: kloss subst. ~en ~ar') — a tell that they knew it was weaker. Per the brief: osäker -> ESCALATE, gissa aldrig. The 'muffin-tin stores Muffinsform' corroboration is suggestive but not decisive (compound stems routinely differ from the free lemma). Operator decides; I will not guess.

summary.zeroRejectsIsAnHonestResult: I did not manufacture a REJECT to justify the pass. I re-tested every value I thought most likely to fall — chess (is schack really neuter?), chips (pluralia tantum?), lilac (does SAOL keep the acute?), clementine (c- or k-?), boots (a pair in the picture), the two dinosaurs (empty/false src) — and each survived. This slice is structurally the safe one: gender and singular are mostly binary or spelling-restoration calls with hard corroboration available in the data itself. The overreach risk in this round lives in the PLURAL slice, where the reviewer repeatedly asserts an -er/-ar declension by ANALOGY while explicitly declining to cite a SAOL entry (eclair, persimmon, flamingo, orangutan, ponny, timer are self-flagged as inferred). That is where a refutation pass should expect to find its rejects; it is not my part.
findings: DEINONYCHUS FALSE CITATION + THE ONLY REAL COUPLING GAP: src='SAOL' but SAOL has no 'deinonychus' entry — the citation is unhonourable, and its identical twin parasaurolophus honestly used src='' for the same unlistable claim. Separately, its coupled plural is neither corrected NOR held, while the twin's IS held — so applying the gender alone yields 'en deinonychus -> flera deinonychus' (utrum + zero plural). For the plural slice, but it must not ship.

CHIPS IS CORROBORATED BY THE FILE ITSELF: sister key 'potato-chips' already ships the identical word 'Chips' with g='t'. The same word carries two genders today; the fix resolves the contradiction. genderSv cannot have produced the 't' (identical input -> identical output), so it is a surviving human value.

COUPLING-GAP HYPOTHESIS RAISED AND THEN REFUTED BY EVIDENCE: all 4 reverse-direction (t->n) gender fixes lack a paired plural correction, which looked like a systematic first-round oversight. It is not — 3 of the 4 (garden-fork, hemlock-tree, parasaurolophus) have their plural deliberately HELD in held-sv.json with honest 'the defect is certain; the replacement form is not' reasoning. Only deinonychus is a genuine gap. Reporting the refutation because a refutation pass that only reports its confirmed suspicions is not doing its job.

EVERY MECHANISM CLAIM IN THIS SLICE IS TRUE, TESTED NOT TRUSTED: I re-implemented genderSv's lookup against the real SV_ETT_WORDS/SV_ETT_SUFFIXES. 'trädgårdsgrep' endsWith 'rep' and 'hemlock' endsWith 'lock' — both false-'t' causes the reviewers NAMED and got exactly right. Better, it explains the dinosaurs they could not: 'deinonychus' and 'parasaurolophus' both end in 'hus', which is why exactly those 2 of 25 dinosaur keys broke while allosaurus/stegosaurus/triceratops match nothing and correctly got 'n'. And 'ufo' is 3 characters, below the suffix loop's length>4 gate, so it fell straight through.
